title: Ibn Khaldun
summary: Ibn Khaldun (1332–1406) was a North African Arab scholar, historian, jurist, and statesman born in Tunis who formulated revolutionary foundations for sociology, historiography, and political economy. In his magnum opus, the Muqaddimah (Prolegomena), written in North Africa before his later career as chief judge in Cairo, he introduced the concept of asabiyyah (social cohesion) to explain the cyclical rise, consolidation, and decline of tribal dynasties and sedentary empires.

uncertainty.note: Born 27 May 1332 (1 Ramadan 732 AH) in Tunis; died 17 March 1406 (26 Ramadan 808 AH) in Cairo.

as_recorded.value: Ibn Khaldūn was born in Tunis on 27 May 1332 /1 Ramaḍān 732... died while in office on 26 Ramaḍān 808/17 March 1406. He was buried in the Sufi cemetery outside Bāb al-Naṣr, Cairo

importance.justification: Ibn Khaldun pioneered scientific historiography, sociology, and political economy, analyzing the social dynamics of nomadic and urban civilizations.
